task: Alternatives to NOAA nClimGrid-Daily for daily highs, lows and precipitation per location; comparison with GHCN-Daily Billings Logan airport for 2025-06-15 and July 2025.
bottom_line: No alternative should replace nClimGrid-Daily. Two can supplement it under conditions: gridMET (4 km; author waiver of copyright; data through 2026-10-17; no-login OPeNDAP subsets) and Daymet (1 km; 1980 to 2025-12-31; no-login single-pixel API; license runs through the DOE-sponsored ORNL record and needs confirmation). PRISM is freely reproducible with attribution, but Oregon State University keeps ownership, so it does not meet the public-domain preference. The S3 by_station CSV named in the task is stale (last TMAX 2025-02-06), so the 2025 check used the current GHCN .dly. At Billings on 2025-06-15 the grids read from -3.0 to +1.2 F against the airport high of 82.9 F (gridMET tmin is 5.7 F low); every grid's July 2025 total was 0.56 to 0.84 in above the airport total of 0.95 in.
recommendation: Do not replace nClimGrid-Daily. Supplement, in this order: (1) gridMET, for 4 km daily tmax, tmin and precipitation up to the latest days, using OPeNDAP cell subsets (no login, no bulk download). Legal basis: the author statement "This work (METDATA, by John Abatzoglou) is free of known copyright restrictions." with the copyright waiver, plus attribution. Record the PRISM dependence and the midnight-MST day. (2) Daymet, as a 1 km per-location cross-check through 2025-12-31, only after the ORNL/DOE license is confirmed in writing and the single-pixel API terms are confirmed; no bulk netCDF pulls in CI (they need Earthdata Login). Legal basis so far: the Earthdata record "openly shared, without restriction", which the EOSDIS guidance says is subject to the sponsoring organization license. (3) Do not ship PRISM as a layer. It may be used internally as a check with attribution, but OSU retains ownership, which fails the public-domain preference in decision 7 unless counsel accepts the free-distribution grant. (4) NOAA normals and Climate at a Glance are context only (county or 30-year normals), not per-location history.
method: Live HTTP requests with curl through the configured proxy, each saved to a per-source downloads folder, with HTTP status, byte count and content checks recorded. Grids read with numpy using the BIL headers and geotransforms; gridMET read through OPeNDAP ASCII subsets with CF scale and offset applied; Daymet read from the single-pixel CSV; GHCN read from the current fixed-width .dly file. Every terms quotation was checked against the saved source text (23 of 23 found). Downloads were deleted after the record was written.

terms.quote: Data. All data (gridded, polygon, tabular, graphical) retrieved from this website or otherwise provided on the website may be freely reproduced and distributed.
terms.reading: Free reproduction and distribution is permitted by the site's own terms. No commercial-use clause appears on the page.

terms.quote: References to the Data. When the data are used, any description should clearly and prominently state, at a minimum, our name, URL, and the date of data access.
terms.reading: Attribution (name, URL, access date) is required for any use.

terms.quote: Copyright and Ownership. All data and information presented through this website are protected by United States copyright laws and applicable international copyright treaties. The PRISM Group, Oregon State University retains rights to ownership of the data and information.
terms.reading: Oregon State University keeps ownership and copyright. PRISM is therefore not public domain, which conflicts with the public-domain preference in the project's decision 7 unless counsel accepts the free-distribution grant.

terms.quote: Disclaimers. It is not recommended that PRISM data be used to calculate very long-term trends.
terms.reading: The site itself advises against long-term trend use.

terms.quote: Map Graphics. Map graphics may be freely reproduced and distributed, as long as the PRISM Group copyright notice, URL, and the date of map creation are reproduced in full.
terms.reading: A separate clause for map images (not gridded data); it requires a copyright notice on any image.

terms.quote: It is important to note that preliminary data fetched in this manner do not account for the fact that we produce 8 versions of a daily grid (and 7 versions of a monthly grid), out to six months, at which point we call it "final."
terms.reading: Automated fetches can return provisional grids. Daily grids change over six months before they are final.

terms.quote: Before downloading data, be sure to acquaint yourself with our terms of use, which explain how to acknowledge any use of our data.
terms.reading: The web service points back to the terms page for attribution.

terms.quote: Data older than six months are considered stable and should not change until a new time series version is released.
terms.reading: Grids older than six months are treated as stable by PRISM.

terms.quote: This dataset is openly shared, without restriction, in accordance with the EOSDIS Data Use and Citation Guidance.
terms.reading: The Daymet V4 R1 record states no restriction, by reference to the EOSDIS guidance below. That guidance defers to the sponsoring organization's license for non-NASA data.

terms.quote: Non-NASA data available through the ESDIS project is subject to the license arrangements of the sponsoring organization. Users are encouraged to validate the source and associated use permissions.
terms.reading: Daymet is an ORNL product, not a NASA-led mission. Its license is the sponsoring organization's license, which was not located as text in this run.

terms.quote: Unless the content is marked with a use restriction or license, data provided from a NASA-led mission are licensed as Creative Commons Zero (CC0). While there are no restrictions on the use of these data, data users are very strongly urged to cite the data used in their work products.
terms.reading: The CC0 default applies to NASA-led mission data. Applying it to Daymet is not established by this text (unverified).

terms.quote: The continued development of the Daymet algorithm and processing is also supported by the Office of Biological and Environmental Research within the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Science.
terms.reading: Names the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science as a co-sponsor, so DOE/ORNL terms are the ones to confirm.

terms.quote: To the extent possible under law, John Abatzoglou has waived all copyright and related or neighboring rights to gridMET.
terms.reading: The author waives copyright to the extent the law allows (a CC0-style waiver statement on the product page).

terms.quote: This work (METDATA, by John Abatzoglou) is free of known copyright restrictions.
terms.reading: States no known copyright restrictions. Written as a page statement, not a separate license file (noted as an open question).

terms.quote: gridMET is semi-operational product that we provide to the community pro-bono and update daily.
terms.reading: Provided free to the community; the service is not contractually guaranteed.

terms.quote: gridMET blends spatial attributes of gridded climate data from PRISM with desirable temporal attributes (and additional variables) from regional reanalysis (NLDAS-2) using climatically aided interpolation.
terms.reading: gridMET is not independent of PRISM: it uses PRISM spatial patterns.

terms.quote: We caution against using gridMET to infer changes in precipitation intensity and frequency.
terms.reading: Precipitation caveat from the producer.

terms.quote: Data for dates within the last 60 days are considered preliminary and subject to change.
terms.reading: Recent gridMET values can change for 60 days after they are written.

terms.quote: gridMET nominally considers a "day" to be midnight-to-midnight Mountain Standard Time (7 UTC)
terms.reading: The gridMET day is midnight MST (07 UTC), which is 1 a.m. MDT in June.

terms.quote: Days correspond approximately to calendar days ending at midnight, Mountain Standard Time (7 UTC the next calendar day)
terms.reading: Same day convention, stated in the NetCDF attributes.

terms.quote: The information on National Weather Service (NWS) Web pages are in the public domain, unless specifically noted otherwise, and may be used without charge for any lawful purpose so long as you do not:
terms.reading: Public-domain statement for NWS web pages only. It does not state the terms for NCEI datasets (GHCN-Daily, normals, Climate at a Glance).

terms.quote: While these data are available to the public, it can be difficult to download and work with such large data volumes.
terms.reading: A public-availability statement, not a license. Not used as a legal basis.

terms.quote: They were first released in May 2021 (v1.0.0), and the statistics for 23 of the sites were reissued in 2023 (v1.0.1).
terms.reading: Version history of the 1991 to 2020 normals (context only).
